maria: heads up — on the long-context QA run (seq=8192) i'm seeing KV cache memory climb steadily and periodic 80-120ms p99 token latency spikes. repro on dedicated staging GPU pool.

kevin: can you share timeline + model + quantization? which eviction policy is active (LRU/FIFO)?

maria: model=redwood/gptx-70b-q4f, quant=q4f, batching heuristic set for low latency, kv_policy=LRU (default). mem tops out +2.5GB over ~1hr then eviction churn kicks in, latency spikes correlate with churn windows.

suneel: does the spike line up with KV paging logs? can you grab runtime.profile and kv.stats?

maria: yes — excerpt pasted: ```
KV_STATS: active_slots=124000
frag_bytes=1.2GB
total_kv_bytes=3.8GB
EVICT_POLICY=LRU
EVICT_CYCLES=13:02:45 intense
```

percy: frag_bytes that high suggests fragmentation from mixed context lengths. we saw similar when reuse_rate low and small-cache-size configured. what's reuse_ratio?

maria: reuse_ratio ~= 0.12 (low) — lot of one-off long chats creating unique prefixes, so cache reuse is poor.

kevin: could be hysteresis in eviction loop — LRU scanning too deep then evicting cold entries which get re-populated, causing churn. FIFO sometimes behaves more stably under high churn. we should A/B.

suneel: i'll run a traffic-replay A/B on staging. enable kv-trace:level=debug so we can capture each evict decision and page-in timings.

maria: started A/B: group A = LRU, group B = FIFO. preliminary: FIFO group shows fewer 100ms+ p99 token spikes, but avg throughput slightly lower. attaching short perf slice: ```
time,policy,alloc_rate_mb_s,evict_count,page_in_count,p99_token_ms
00:00,Lru,12.4,432,210,118
00:00,Fifo,11.8,210,240,62
00:15,Lru,13.1,980,450,132
00:15,Fifo,12.0,430,520,68
```

kevin: important to validate correctness — FIFO mustn't break KV lookup semantics. any incorrect outputs or hallucinations correlated with policy change?

maria: ran deterministic prompt set (eval-suite v3) against both groups — no correctness diffs observed. FIFO has higher miss rate but outputs are equivalent.

percy: also consider interaction with kernel selection/batching. if eviction happens on hot path while kernel chooses blocked kernels, that can amplify latency. can we offload eviction to background worker with bounded pause?

suneel: background eviction reduced blocking in earlier experiments but increased fragmentation because evictions are more asynchronous. maybe tune min_resident_pages + scan_window to balance.

maria: filed issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/1234 — proposed plan:
1) run extended 24h A/B to measure long-term mem growth and p99 stability
2) add kv-usage heatmap (per-slot hotness over time) and detailed evict traces
3) try FIFO + background-evict + smaller scan window and compare

deploy-bot: canary started for fifo-policy on staging-pool-3 at 2026-01-17T09:10Z

kevin: thanks — can someone add a tiny python repro that simulates long unique-context churn (many unique prefixes, occasional reuse) so we can run locally and iterate faster? i'll take it if not claimed.

maria: thanks all — will attach 6h profile dump and heap map once available. :thumbsup:
